summary: Describes the Voice Profile for Internet Mail (VPIM) directory service, which finds the email address of a recipient from a telephone number. It can also provide a spoken name and the recipient's media capabilities, giving voice mail users a familiar experience. It merges two earlier documents into one working group submission.

plainLanguage.summary: A phone book for voice messages. Give it a phone number and it tells you the mailbox address, and maybe lets you hear the person say their name, so you know you have the right one.

questions: find email address from phone number
what is the vpim directory service
how to look up voicemail address by phone number
subtitle: A directory schema that turns a telephone number into a voice mailbox address, a spoken name and capabilities.

tldr.problem: A sender of voice mail knows only the recipient's telephone number. Internet mail needs an email address, and the sender also wants some assurance that the message will be delivered as intended.
tldr.mechanism: The VPIM directory service defines an LDAP auxiliary object class, vPIMUser, with attributes for the mailbox address, an optional spoken name and the recipient's media capabilities. A client looks up an entry by telephone number.
tldr.outcome: A sender can confirm the right person by voice and learn what the recipient accepts before sending. Service providers must weigh the privacy risk of exposing subscriber data.

today: RFC 4237 is a Proposed Standard. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, so it remains the definition of the VPIM directory schema.

sections.title: Scope and Design Goals
sections.content:
The VPIM directory schema (VPIMDIR) is a directory service for the Voice Profile for Internet Mail (VPIM). It is accessed from outside the enterprise or service provider domain, using the recipient's telephone number. Given that number, it returns the recipient's email address. Optionally it also returns the spoken name of the recipient and the recipient's media capabilities.

The aim is to recreate the voice mail user experience with standardized directories. At addressing time the sender gets basic assurances that the message will be delivered as intended.
sections.plainLanguage: When you call a friend's voice mailbox you want to be sure it is really theirs. This service lets the sender check first, before leaving the message.

sections.title: Performance, Scaling and Reliability Constraints
sections.content:
The query is expected to use LDAP, a connection-oriented protocol. The transaction needs several packet round-trips and is considered the highest latency element of the messaging service. Retrieving the spoken name may mean returning up to 20kbytes (5 seconds at 4kbytes/second). The RFC believes a 1250 ms response time is achievable over the Internet at large, given a sufficiently engineered connection.

A service provider's namespace is expected to hold tens of millions of subscribers in a flat namespace of the form telephone_number@domain_name. A large corporation may have a hundred-thousand entries. Existing directory technology, including replication, is believed to give enough throughput. The one fundamentally new requirement is returning the spoken name, which adds to storage needs more than to latency.

DNS offers redundancy and load balancing for locating the service. However, the latency requirements may not allow client-side fail-over to a secondary server, so the directory server may need to be a high-availability service.
sections.plainLanguage: Looking someone up has to be fast, even when the phone book has millions of names. So the people who run it need to make it very reliable.

sections.title: The vPIMUser Object Class
sections.content:
The schema defines one auxiliary object class, vPIMUser, which can be attached to a directory entry. It has two required attributes, vPIMRfc822Mailbox and vPIMTelephoneNumber. It has eight optional ones: vPIMSpokenName, vPIMSupportedUABehaviors, vPIMSupportedAudioMediaTypes, vPIMSupportedMessageContext, vPIMTextName, vPIMExtendedAbsenceStatus, vPIMMaxMessageSize and vPIMSubMailboxes.

When present, the object holds information for verifying that the dialed number matches the intended recipient. It also carries capability and mailbox status information that helps the sender compose the message and set delivery expectations.
sections.plainLanguage: Think of an index card with two must-have lines, the phone number and the mailbox address, and several optional lines like a recorded name.

sections.title: Telephone Number and Mailbox Address
sections.content:
vPIMTelephoneNumber is the full E.164 form of the telephone number, including any sub-addressing portion, and is the attribute normally searched. It is stored with no parentheses, spaces, dots or hyphens. The leading + and the + that separates the submailbox are required markup. The RFC's example is a North American number with sub-address 12, written +12145551212+12.

The attribute is multi-valued by default, but multiple values MUST be distinct in the telephone number portion. Each submailbox of a number is expected to have its own vPIMUser entry. It differs from LDAP's telephoneNumber in supporting sub-addressing and in being used as a voice messaging address.

vPIMRfc822Mailbox stores the inter-domain SMTP address of the voice mailbox. It is a separate attribute from rfc822Mailbox, which may be used for other purposes. It is not a subtype only because some directory implementations do not support subtyping.
sections.plainLanguage: The phone number is the thing you look up, written in one strict format. The answer is the email-style address where the voice message should be sent.

sections.title: Names and Capability Attributes
sections.content:
vPIMSpokenName is an octet string that MUST be encoded in 32 kbit/s ADPCM exactly, containing the user's name in the user's own voice. It MUST NOT exceed five seconds. vPIMTextName is a text name consistent with the databases used for calling name delivery in caller ID.

vPIMSupportedAudioMediaTypes lists the audio encodings the mailbox can receive, using MIME audio subtypes registered with IANA. Private types must be prefixed X- or x-. Because ADPCM is a required format, audio32kadpcm must be listed if the attribute is present. vPIMSupportedMessageContext gives coarser guidance on the message contexts the recipient is likely to accept, with values defined in the message context RFC.

vPIMSupportedUABehaviors lists optional features the recipient supports: MessageDispositionNotification, MessageSensitivity and MessageImportance. If the attribute is absent, only features mandatory in VPIM are assumed. vPIMMaxMessageSize gives the maximum message length in seconds, because a byte limit is an unreliable guide when several encodings are supported. vPIMSubMailboxes lists sub-mailbox numbers in the range 1-9999, which can drive a post-dial menu.
sections.plainLanguage: The optional lines say how the person sounds, what kinds of audio their mailbox understands, and how long a message it can hold.

sections.title: Extended Absence Status
sections.content:
vPIMExtendedAbsenceStatus is a single-valued attribute that works like a vacation notice for voice mail. It gives the sender an advisory message at sending time. Three values are defined.

  • Off: the recipient does not support extended absence or has not set it. This is the default when the attribute is not returned.
  • On: an extended absence is set, but the mailbox still accepts messages for review at an unspecified future time.
  • MsgBlocked: an extended absence is set and the mailbox rejects incoming messages. Messages SHOULD NOT be sent if this value is returned.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a sign on the mailbox door: open, away but still taking notes, or please do not leave anything.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC lists three known issues. First, customer information is sensitive, and because telephone numbers are densely assigned, repeated LDAP queries can be used to harvest a list of active subscribers. Providers may therefore withhold data useful for telemarketing, such as the text name, and disclose only what helps the sender, such as the spoken name, which is much harder to process automatically.

Second, many countries have privacy laws that prohibit disclosing some descriptive information such as text names. Server implementors are encouraged to support DIT structural rules and name forms, and administrators to use access controls to restrict attributes holding sensitive data.

Third, the service gives unauthenticated, public access to directory data. It is therefore vulnerable to attacks that redirect the query to a rogue server that offers malicious data.
sections.plainLanguage: A public phone book can be abused to collect everyone's details or to give you fake answers, so the owners should limit what they show and protect the service.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA has registered an LDAP object identifier that serves as the base for all schema elements in the document. It has also registered the LDAP descriptors, one object class (vPIMUser) and ten attributes. The schema text itself shows each element under a placeholder IANA-ASSIGNED-OID prefix, so the actual numbers are assigned by the registry rather than written in the RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: The official list of names and numbers was updated so everyone uses the same labels for these fields.

viz.caption: WHAT A VPIMUSER ENTRY CAN HOLD

items.title: Required: telephone number
items.text: vPIMTelephoneNumber, in E.164 form with optional sub-address.

items.title: Spoken name
items.text: 32 kbit/s ADPCM, at most five seconds.

items.title: Media capabilities
items.text: Audio types, message context and optional user agent behaviors.

items.title: Mailbox status
items.text: Extended absence, maximum message size and sub-mailboxes.
